html:
SMTO-TSK-0027 — That task button doesn't apply to the task right now

GUID: 70ed238d-867f-4f35-9ef0-64edcff3b010
Slug: task-action-state-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The task changed after the button was shown. It may have finished, stopped, paused or already started, so SMTO didn't carry out this action.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the conversation again so the task shows its current status and buttons. The button you pressed was based on an older view of the task.
  2. Check whether your action already happened: for example the task is already retrying, paused, stopped, resumed, or gone from the Queued list. Pressing it again could repeat work that has already started.
  3. Only if it didn't happen, use a button the task shows now, such as Resume, Continue task, Retry or Run next. If you typed a command like /pause or /resume, check the task's status first. SMTO only shows the buttons that fit the task's current state, and commands only work when the task is in the right state.
  4. If the task is paused and you want to answer it, select Resume first, then reply. A paused task can't take answers until it is resumed.

What success looks like

  • The task shows the status you expected, such as running, paused or stopped, and the action happened only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which button you pressed. Don't keep pressing task buttons until you know what state the task is in.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A task control (retry, continue, resume, pause, stop, run next, edit/remove, confirmation answer or slash command) was rejected because the task's current status, ownership, pause/approval state or queue position does not allow it.

What this means

  • A task control is incompatible with current status, ownership, pending approval/pause, queue membership or continuation eligibility. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A task control is incompatible with current status, ownership, pending approval/pause, queue membership or continuation eligibility.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the action-specific rejection and current controls; shared classification does not imply a failed task should always be retried.

How to fix it

  • Read the specific rejection in Technical details (for example "Only a failed conversation task can be retried", "Continue task requires a stopped or interrupted run" or "Resume the paused task before responding or continuing"). Re-read the task and conversation-lane state, use only the actions listed in the run snapshot's lifecycle actions, and confirm whether a prior attempt already took effect before sending another control.
  • Refresh the task and use the action currently offered by its conversation lane. Confirm the prior attempt’s receipts and unresolved effects before any new execution.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended action is offered for current authoritative state with prior effects reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
